decision_note: CORRECTS PR #379's group 83. #379 read the two NPS rows as an intra-NPS duplicate and proposed a 3-way merge to the OR visitor row. Reading the descriptions reverses that: nps:place:84986DF5 ('Hat Rock') is the basalt formation and says so — 'a formation of exposed basalt that rises approximately 70 feet... It is located within the 719-acre Hat Rock State Park' — while nps:place:2E2CB476 ('Hat Rock State Park') describes the park's pond, boat access and volleyball court. The shared npmapId that suggested a duplicate is a Lewis-and-Clark-trail identifier, not a place id: 299 distinct NPS place records share it, and 4,555 NPS place records carry only 37 distinct npmapIds. efe59e93 (the state_parks polygon, never in #379's group) is added as canonical; the rock is excluded. See docs/investigations/2026-09-04-group-6-and-83.md.

decision_note: NET-NEW group, not an edit to group 6. Group 6 (02106f71 SRA-visitor vs 79c97694 atlas 'Salton Sea') stays DIFFERENT and is NOT merged: the atlas row describes the saline lake ('about 15 miles wide and 35 miles long'), the visitor row describes a 15,000-acre park unit on its northeast shore. 79c97694 appears nowhere in this file. That atlas id is named here only to record the decision — it is deliberately absent from every functional field (canonical_mp_id, absorbed_mp_ids, excluded_ids, member_sides) of every group in this file. This group instead pairs the SRA visitor row with the SRA's own state_parks record, which the classifier never grouped: their names differ by abbreviation (trigram similarity 0.323 between 'Salton Sea State Recreation Area' and 'Salton Sea SRA') and their centroids are 13,078.4 m apart because the state_parks centroid is the centroid of a multi-part shoreline polygon. The visitor point sits 7.7 m outside that polygon. See docs/investigations/2026-09-04-group-6-and-83.md.
